description: Penicillium is a genus of fungi commonly found in soil, air, and decaying organic matter. Many species cause post-harvest diseases in fruits and vegetables, producing blue or green molds and leading to significant storage losses.
symptoms: Soft watery rot on fruits or plant tissues
Blue-green or green powdery mold on infected areas
visual_symptoms: blue or green mold growth on fruit surface
soft rotting tissue around infection site
spread: Contact between infected and healthy produce
impact: Loss of product quality during storage
Potential production of mycotoxins in some species
management: Handle fruits carefully to avoid wounds
Store produce at recommended temperature and humidity
biological_control: Use of beneficial microbes such as Bacillus species
Application of antagonistic yeasts to suppress mold growth
chemical_control: Post-harvest fungicides such as thiabendazole or imazalil
Use of approved storage fungicides depending on crop
prevention: Maintain cold chain for perishable crops
source: Plant pathology literature on post-harvest diseases
